ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-lingual rater trained on translation-consistent labels
PROPOSAL: Take 2M English web documents scored by two different open 7B instruction models, keep those where the two scores agree, and machine-translate 200000 of them into 11 languages to obtain label-consistent training pairs. Train a 3-layer perceptron head on a frozen multilingual encoder and measure rank correlation of its scores on 5000 parallel documents. No benchmark-derived positives are used.
CONTROLS: A rater trained on English only and applied zero-shot, a language-identity probe on the learned scores to test whether language leaks into quality, and a FastText classifier trained on the same documents.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Agreement on parallel documents should exceed that of the English-only rater. It could fail if translation noise dominates in low-resource languages, which would lower the rank correlation there.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-tuned multilingual encoder rater from prompt-based quality scores
PROPOSAL: Take 1M English web documents scored by one open 3B instruction model under varied prompt wordings, and machine-translate a sample of them into 5 languages. Fine-tune a 560M-parameter multilingual encoder end to end, with 5 seeds and a validation-tuned schedule, and measure rank correlation of its scores on 2000 parallel documents. Report the language-identity probe accuracy on the penultimate layer.
CONTROLS: A rater trained on English only and applied zero-shot, a FastText classifier trained on the same documents, and a rater fine-tuned on shuffled scores as a control for generic adaptation.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Agreement on parallel documents should be high for the prompt variants that share a rubric. It could fail if the variants disagree in the translated languages, which would show the rater inherits the judge's idiosyncrasies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Downstream effect of multilingual selection on 1B proxy models
PROPOSAL: Pretrain 1B-parameter decoder models on 30B tokens drawn from 6 languages under five selection rules: random sampling, heuristic filtering only, a benchmark-derived rater, an English-trained rater applied after translation, and the proposed multilingual rater keeping the top 20 percent. Evaluate on XNLI, Belebele, translated MMLU and 4 English tasks, with 2 seeds for the random and proposed arms and a learning rate set once on validation loss. The question is whether the quality signal improves downstream performance in English and in other languages.
CONTROLS: Matched token counts and tokenizer for every arm, a random sample filtered by document length alone, and a model trained on the same budget of unfiltered text with deduplication.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The proposed rater should lead on the non-English tasks and match the English-trained rater in English. It could fail if differences stay within seed noise at this model size, in which case a larger run would be needed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Selection ratio study for a 3B proxy model on English-language benchmarks
PROPOSAL: Pretrain 3B-parameter decoder models on 10B tokens from 2 languages, keeping the top 25 percent of documents ranked by the proposed multilingual rater or all of them, with 3 seeds, and run a 14B judge model on 5000 sampled documents to audit the kept text. Evaluate on XNLI, Belebele, translated MMLU and 4 English tasks. The question is how the kept fraction changes downstream results. Report scores by language family and by task type, and keep the selected documents for later reading.
CONTROLS: Matched token counts and tokenizer for the arms, a random sample filtered by document length alone, and a model trained on unfiltered text with deduplication at the same token count.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Intermediate ratios should beat both extremes on the benchmarks. It could fail if the ratio matters little, which would leave the rater's value to the choice of language mix.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Language invariance of quality scores on parallel text
PROPOSAL: Score the FLORES-200 sentences and 3000 machine-translated web documents in 8 languages with the proposed rater and with an English-only rater, and compute the shift in score after translation. Report rank correlation of scores for the same document in different languages and fit a regression of score shift on script and resource level. The aim is to see whether judgments depend on content rather than on the language of writing.
CONTROLS: A length-matched random score as a null, a perplexity filter scored on the same text, and a rater applied to documents translated twice to separate translation noise from language effects.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Rank correlation for the proposed rater should exceed that of the English-only rater and the shift should be small. It could fail if low-resource scripts show a consistent offset, which would point to leakage of language.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Round-trip translation audit of rater consistency in two scripts
PROPOSAL: Take 3000 web documents in Hindi and Russian, translate them to English with a 7B translation model and back, and score the original, the English version and the round-trip version with the proposed rater, 5 seeds of the rater head. Report rank correlation among the three versions and fit a regression of score change on document length and domain. This shows how far scores track content. Embed the documents and relate score to the first embedding axis.
CONTROLS: A length-matched random score as a null, a perplexity filter scored on the same text, and a rater applied to documents translated by two different systems.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Round-trip scores should correlate strongly with the originals. It could fail if domain explains most of the change, in which case consistency would reflect topic rather than language.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Benchmark contamination audit of the selected corpora
PROPOSAL: Run 13-gram overlap and embedding nearest-neighbour search between the documents kept by the proposed rater, a benchmark-derived rater and random sampling, and the test sets of Belebele, XNLI and translated MMLU in 6 languages. Report the count of flagged documents per million and compare the arms. The aim is to check that supervision free of benchmarks lowers the risk of test-set contamination.
CONTROLS: A planted-contamination test where 500 benchmark items are inserted into the pool to measure detection recall, a threshold sweep on the embedding similarity, and the same audit on the unfiltered pool.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The benchmark-derived rater should keep more flagged documents than the proposed one. It could fail if overlap is rare in all arms, in which case the audit would not separate them.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sensitivity of a small model to injected benchmark documents
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 500M-parameter decoder on 8B tokens of text kept by the proposed rater, with test items from Belebele and XNLI injected at 3 duplication levels, and measure the gain on the injected items with 5 seeds. Fit the gain against the duplication level and report the level at which the gain is detectable above noise. The aim is to calibrate how much contamination would matter.
CONTROLS: A model trained on the same text without injection, a model trained on text kept at random with the same injection, and a threshold sweep on the 13-gram detector.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Gain should rise with duplication and become visible at the highest level. It could fail if the model is too small to memorise at these levels, which would make the calibration uninformative.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling several judges into one multilingual classifier
PROPOSAL: Score 1M multilingual web documents with three prompt-based judges, a 14B instruction model, a 7B model and an educational-value prompt, average their rank scores, and distil the average into a 100M-parameter multilingual classifier. Compare the classifier's agreement with each judge and with the average on 5000 held-out documents in 10 languages. The aim is to reduce the model-specific bias of any one judge.
CONTROLS: A classifier distilled from each judge alone, a majority label from the judges as an alternative target, and a language-identity probe on the classifier scores.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The classifier trained on the average should agree more evenly with all judges than any single-judge classifier. It could fail if the judges disagree mostly on content type, which would make the average a blend rather than a consensus.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distillation of one judge at three classifier sizes
PROPOSAL: Score 500000 multilingual web documents with one 7B instruction model and distil the scores into classifiers of 30M, 100M and 300M parameters, 8 seeds. Compare agreement with the judge on 5000 held-out documents in 4 languages and fit a power law of agreement against classifier size. Report calibration by language and keep the score distributions for inspection. This shows how small a rater can be.
CONTROLS: A classifier trained on the judge's binary labels instead of ranks, a majority label from a second prompt as an alternative target, and a language-identity probe on the classifier scores.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Agreement should rise slowly with size and saturate near the 100M model. It could fail if calibration differs by language, which would tie the result to the language mix.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Kept-fraction sweep for multilingual selection at moderate scale
PROPOSAL: Pretrain 500M-parameter decoder models on 10B tokens from 5 languages, keeping the top 10, 20, 40 and 80 percent of documents ranked by the proposed rater, and compare with a random sample and a heuristic filter at matching token counts. Evaluate on Belebele, XNLI, translated MMLU and 3 English tasks, 3 seeds for the 20 percent arm and a learning rate fixed on validation loss. The sweep shows how much selection pays before diversity starts to drop.
CONTROLS: A random sample at every token count, a diversity audit through the number of distinct domains and languages kept, and a run at the 20 percent ratio with a rater trained on a different seed.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Moderate ratios should give the best average score and the strictest ratio should lose diversity. It could fail if all ratios sit within noise, in which case the sweep would not locate an optimum.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Judge-size comparison for prompt-based multilingual quality labels
PROPOSAL: Compare quality labels from a 3B and a 14B instruction model on 20000 multilingual web documents in 12 languages, then train a 100M-parameter classifier on both label sets and pretrain 1B-parameter decoders on 20B tokens of the text the classifiers keep, 3 seeds. Evaluate on Belebele, XNLI and 3 English tasks. Report agreement of the two label sets by language and by document domain, and keep the disagreements for manual reading. The question is whether a larger judge yields a better selection signal.
CONTROLS: A random sample at matched token counts, a classifier trained on labels from the two judges combined, and an audit of the labels by language to find where the judges disagree.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The larger judge should help on low-resource languages only. It could fail if both selections perform alike, in which case the smaller judge would suffice.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Proposed rater against heuristic and model-based baselines at 3B scale
PROPOSAL: Pretrain 3B-parameter decoder models on 60B tokens from 8 languages under five selection rules: heuristic filtering, a FastText quality classifier, an English-trained educational-value classifier after translation, a benchmark-derived multilingual rater, and the proposed rater, with 2 seeds for the heuristic and proposed arms. Evaluate on XNLI, Belebele, translated MMLU and 6 English tasks. This answers whether the signal beats existing strategies in English and in other languages.
CONTROLS: Matched token counts and tokenizer for all arms, a random sample as a floor, and the heuristic arm with deduplication switched on to keep the comparison tight.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: The proposed rater should lead on non-English tasks and tie in English. It could fail if the benchmark-derived rater wins on its own languages, which would reflect contamination rather than quality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Proposed rater against baselines with larger proxy models and more seeds
PROPOSAL: Pretrain 7B-parameter decoder models on 20B tokens from 3 languages under three selection rules: heuristic filtering, a benchmark-derived multilingual rater, and the proposed rater, with 5 seeds for all arms and a second round of training. Evaluate on XNLI, Belebele and 3 English tasks, and on 12 translated reasoning sets with 3 prompt formats. Report means with intervals and the per-task breakdown for the languages.
CONTROLS: Matched token counts and tokenizer for all arms, a random sample as a floor, and the heuristic arm with deduplication switched on to keep the comparison tight.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: The proposed rater should lead on non-English tasks and tie in English. It could fail if prompt format changes the ranking, which would show the benchmarks are fragile at this scale.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Throughput of candidate raters on web-scale text
PROPOSAL: Measure documents scored per second for a FastText classifier, a 100M-parameter multilingual encoder rater and a prompted 7B instruction model on 1M multilingual web documents, with truncation at 512 tokens, and extrapolate the time for a corpus of 5B documents. Report agreement of each rater with the 7B model on 10000 documents. The check is that the proposed rater is efficient enough for web-scale corpora.
CONTROLS: A batch-size sweep for the encoder, a run with the documents sorted by length against shuffled order, and a check that scores do not change under truncation at 256 tokens.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: The encoder should run orders of magnitude faster than the prompted model while keeping high agreement. It could fail if tokenisation dominates the time, which would mask the model difference.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latency study of a distilled rater at several batch sizes
PROPOSAL: Distil a 100M-parameter multilingual encoder into smaller students of 20M, 40M and 60M parameters on 300000 documents scored by a 7B instruction model, then measure documents scored per second at a batch that fills memory on 1M web documents. Report agreement of each student with the teacher on 10000 documents under the same tokenizer and fit throughput against student size. This shows where speed stops paying.
CONTROLS: A student trained from random initialisation as a control, a quantised version of the 60M student, and a check that scores do not change under truncation at 256 tokens.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: Throughput should rise nearly linearly as students shrink with a slow loss of agreement. It could fail if agreement drops sharply below 40M parameters, which would set a floor on size.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Effect of multilingual selection on English benchmarks
PROPOSAL: Pretrain 1B-parameter decoder models on 20B tokens of English web text kept by the proposed multilingual rater, by an English-trained educational-value classifier, and by random sampling, 3 seeds for the proposed arm. Evaluate on 6 English benchmarks including ARC, HellaSwag and MMLU. The question is whether a rater built for many languages costs anything in English quality compared with an English-only selector.
CONTROLS: Matched token counts and tokenizer for all arms, a rater trained on translated data only as an ablation of supervision type, and an audit of the overlap between kept document sets.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The multilingual rater should land within noise of the English selector. It could fail if its kept set drops technical documents, which would lower the MMLU score.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: English benchmark comparison with a rater trained on translated documents
PROPOSAL: Pretrain 3B-parameter decoder models on 12B tokens of English web text kept by the proposed multilingual rater and by random sampling, 5 seeds for the proposed arm, and measure change in score at 4 checkpoints. Evaluate on 8 English benchmarks including ARC, HellaSwag and MMLU, with scores read under 3 prompt templates. The question is whether selection helps English performance.
CONTROLS: Matched token counts and tokenizer for all arms, a rater trained on translated data only as an ablation of supervision type, and an audit of the overlap between kept document sets and a training-set sample.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The proposed arm should beat random sampling on knowledge tasks. It could fail if templates reorder the arms, in which case the gain would not be reliable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer of the rater to low-resource languages
PROPOSAL: Apply the proposed rater to web text in 6 low-resource languages and continue pretraining a 500M-parameter multilingual decoder on 3B tokens of the top half of each language, comparing with random sampling at the same token count, 3 seeds. Evaluate on Belebele and XNLI in those languages. The test is whether the selection signal helps where labelled quality data are scarce.
CONTROLS: Language-specific heuristic filters as an alternative, a rater whose encoder is replaced by a smaller one to test the role of capacity, and an audit of script and domain balance in the kept text.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Selection should give a measurable gain on Belebele for most languages. It could fail if encoder coverage of these scripts is weak, which would make the scores close to random.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continued pretraining with the rater on two lower-resource languages
PROPOSAL: Apply the proposed rater to web text in Swahili and Tamil and continue pretraining a 1B-parameter multilingual decoder on 4B tokens of the top 30 percent of Swahili and Tamil text, 8 seeds, with 3 sampling temperatures, comparing with random sampling. Evaluate on Belebele and XNLI in those languages. Report the share of documents kept by script and domain. This tests whether the selection signal helps there.
CONTROLS: Language-specific heuristic filters as an alternative, a rater whose encoder is replaced by a larger one, and an audit of script balance in the kept text.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Selection should give a small gain on Belebele. It could fail if the sampling temperature changes the sign of the gain, which would make the effect depend on tuning.
